From fb7fb4016300ac622c964069e286dc83166a5d52 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 23:28:15 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nf_tables: clone set on flush only

Syzbot with fault injection triggered a failing memory allocation with
GFP_KERNEL which results in a WARN splat:

iter.err
WARNING: net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:845 at nft_map_deactivate+0x34e/0x3c0 net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:845, CPU#0: syz.0.17/5992
Modules linked in:
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 5992 Comm: syz.0.17 Not tainted syzkaller #0 PREEMPT(full)
Hardware name: Google Google Compute Engine/Google Compute Engine, BIOS Google 02/12/2026
RIP: 0010:nft_map_deactivate+0x34e/0x3c0 net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:845
Code: 8b 05 86 5a 4e 09 48 3b 84 24 a0 00 00 00 75 62 48 8d 65 d8 5b 41 5c 41 5d 41 5e 41 5f 5d c3 cc cc cc cc cc e8 63 6d fa f7 90 <0f> 0b 90 43
+80 7c 35 00 00 0f 85 23 fe ff ff e9 26 fe ff ff 89 d9
RSP: 0018:ffffc900045af780 EFLAGS: 00010293
RAX: ffffffff89ca45bd RBX: 00000000fffffff4 RCX: ffff888028111e40
RDX: 0000000000000000 RSI: 00000000fffffff4 RDI: 0000000000000000
RBP: ffffc900045af870 R08: 0000000000400dc0 R09: 00000000ffffffff
R10: dffffc0000000000 R11: fffffbfff1d141db R12: ffffc900045af7e0
R13: 1ffff920008b5f24 R14: dffffc0000000000 R15: ffffc900045af920
FS:  000055557a6a5500(0000) GS:ffff888125496000(0000) knlGS:0000000000000000
CS:  0010 DS: 0000 ES: 0000 CR0: 0000000080050033
CR2: 00007fb5ea271fc0 CR3: 000000003269e000 CR4: 00000000003526f0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 __nft_release_table+0xceb/0x11f0 net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:12115
 nft_rcv_nl_event+0xc25/0xdb0 net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c:12187
 notifier_call_chain+0x19d/0x3a0 kernel/notifier.c:85
 blocking_notifier_call_chain+0x6a/0x90 kernel/notifier.c:380
 netlink_release+0x123b/0x1ad0 net/netlink/af_netlink.c:761
 __sock_release net/socket.c:662 [inline]
 sock_close+0xc3/0x240 net/socket.c:1455

Restrict set clone to the flush set command in the preparation phase.
Add NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE and use it for this purpose, update the rbtree
and pipapo backends to only clone the set when this iteration type is
used.

As for the existing NFT_ITER_UPDATE type, update the pipapo backend to
use the existing set clone if available, otherwise use the existing set
representation. After this update, there is no need to clone a set that
is being deleted, this includes bound anonymous set.

An alternative approach to NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE is to add a .clone
interface and call it from the flush set path.

Reported-by: syzbot+4924a0edc148e8b4b342@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 3f1d886cc7c3 ("netfilter: nft_set_pipapo: move cloning of match info to insert/removal path")
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c b/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
index 7ef4b44471d3..c091898df710 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c
@@ -2144,13 +2144,20 @@ static void nft_pipapo_walk(const struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set *set,
 	const struct nft_pipapo_match *m;
 
 	switch (iter->type) {
-	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:
 		m = pipapo_maybe_clone(set);
 		if (!m) {
 			iter->err = -ENOMEM;
 			return;
 		}
-
+		nft_pipapo_do_walk(ctx, set, m, iter);
+		break;
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+		if (priv->clone)
+			m = priv->clone;
+		else
+			m = rcu_dereference_protected(priv->match,
+						      nft_pipapo_transaction_mutex_held(set));
 		nft_pipapo_do_walk(ctx, set, m, iter);
 		break;
 	case NFT_ITER_READ:

diff --git a/include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h b/include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h
index 426534a711b0..ea6f29ad7888 100644
--- a/include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h
+++ b/include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h
@@ -320,11 +320,13 @@ static inline void *nft_elem_priv_cast(const struct nft_elem_priv *priv)
  * @NFT_ITER_UNSPEC: unspecified, to catch errors
  * @NFT_ITER_READ: read-only iteration over set elements
  * @NFT_ITER_UPDATE: iteration under mutex to update set element state
+ * @NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE: clone set before iteration under mutex to update element
  */
 enum nft_iter_type {
 	NFT_ITER_UNSPEC,
 	NFT_ITER_READ,
 	NFT_ITER_UPDATE,
+	NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE,
 };
 
 struct nft_set;

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c b/net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c
index df67932d3e09..058f7004cb2b 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c
@@ -833,6 +833,11 @@ static void nft_map_catchall_deactivate(const struct nft_ctx *ctx,
 	}
 }
 
+/* Use NFT_ITER_UPDATE iterator even if this may be called from the preparation
+ * phase, the set clone might already exist from a previous command, or it might
+ * be a set that is going away and does not require a clone. The netns and
+ * netlink release paths also need to work on the live set.
+ */
 static void nft_map_deactivate(const struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set *set)
 {
 	struct nft_set_iter iter = {
@@ -7903,9 +7908,12 @@ static int nft_set_catchall_flush(const struct nft_ctx *ctx,
 
 static int nft_set_flush(struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set *set, u8 genmask)
 {
+	/* The set backend might need to clone the set, do it now from the
+	 * preparation phase, use NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE iterator type.
+	 */
 	struct nft_set_iter iter = {
 		.genmask	= genmask,
-		.type		= NFT_ITER_UPDATE,
+		.type		= NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE,
 		.fn		= nft_setelem_flush,
 	};
 

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c b/net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c
index 3f02e4478216..ee3d4f5b9ff7 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c
@@ -861,13 +861,15 @@ static void nft_rbtree_walk(const struct nft_ctx *ctx,
 	struct nft_rbtree *priv = nft_set_priv(set);
 
 	switch (iter->type) {
-	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
-		lockdep_assert_held(&nft_pernet(ctx->net)->commit_mutex);
-
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:
 		if (nft_array_may_resize(set) < 0) {
 			iter->err = -ENOMEM;
 			break;
 		}
+		fallthrough;
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+		lockdep_assert_held(&nft_pernet(ctx->net)->commit_mutex);
+
 		nft_rbtree_do_walk(ctx, set, iter);
 		break;
 	case NFT_ITER_READ:
--

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c b/net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c
index 739b992bde59..b0e571c8e3f3 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c
@@ -374,6 +374,7 @@ static void nft_rhash_walk(const struct nft_ctx *ctx, struct nft_set *set,
 {
 	switch (iter->type) {
 	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:
 		/* only relevant for netlink dumps which use READ type */
 		WARN_ON_ONCE(iter->skip != 0);

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications per File

1. **`include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h`**  
   Added a new enum member `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` to `nft_iter_type`. This distinguishes iteration that requires a set clone (for flush operations) from regular update iteration.

2. **`net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c`**  
   - In `nft_map_deactivate()`: Added a comment explaining that the function now uses `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` intentionally (not the clone variant) to avoid cloning in paths where the set might be going away or already cloned.  
   - In `nft_set_flush()`: Changed the iteration type from `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` so that the set is cloned during the preparation phase, where memory allocation failures are acceptable.

3. **`net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c`**  
   - In `nft_pipapo_walk()` (the pipapo backend walk function):  
     - Added a `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:` that calls `pipapo_maybe_clone()` (allocates a clone) and then does the walk on the clone.  
     - Modified the `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:` to use an existing clone (`priv->clone`) if available, otherwise fall back to the live match. This avoids unnecessary cloning in non‑flush update paths.

4. **`net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c`**  
   - In `nft_rbtree_walk()` (the rbtree backend walk function):  
     - Added a `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:` that first checks if array resize is possible (returns -ENOMEM on failure) and then falls through to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to perform the walk.  
     - The `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:` now only asserts the commit mutex lock and performs the walk without cloning (since cloning is only relevant for the new clone‑type).

5. **`net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c`**  
   - In `nft_rhash_walk()` (the rhashtable backend walk function):  
     - Added `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:` as a fallthrough to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` because the hash backend does not require cloning; it simply skips the same entries for both iteration types.

### Relationships between Modifications

The core fix is driven by the new `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` iteration type. This type is used **only** in the flush‑set command (`nft_set_flush`) to signal that a set clone must be created during the preparation phase. By isolating the clone requirement to a specific iteration type, the patch avoids cloning in other paths that run under memory pressure (e.g., `nft_map_deactivate`, set deletion, or netns release). Each backend (pipapo, rbtree, hash) implements this new type according to its own needs:  
- **Pipapo** must clone to support concurrent updates, so it clones only for `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`.  
- **Rbtree** must check for possible array resize only for the clone type, then falls through to the normal update handling.  
- **Hash** treats both types identically (no clone needed).  

The change in `nft_map_deactivate` ensures that it uses `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` (the regular update type) instead of the clone type, preventing the memory allocation failure that caused the WARN splat. This is safe because either a clone already exists from a previous flush command, or the set is being removed and does not need a clone.  

Overall, the patch tightly couples the clone operation to the flush preparation phase, reducing the risk of allocation failures in other code paths.

### Modifications per File

1. **`include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h`**  
   - Added a new enum value `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` to `enum nft_iter_type`. This distinguishes flush operations (which require set cloning during the preparation phase) from regular updates.

2. **`net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c`**  
   - In `nft_set_flush()`, changed the iterator type from `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` so that the set backend clones the set during the preparation phase when flushing.

3. **`net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c`**

   - In `nft_pipapo_walk()`, split handling of `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` from `NFT_ITER_UPDATE`.  
     - For `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`: calls `pipapo_maybe_clone()` to clone the set; if cloning fails, sets `iter->err` and returns. Then performs the walk on the clone.  
     - For `NFT_ITER_UPDATE`: if a clone already exists (`priv->clone`), uses the clone; otherwise uses the live match (under the transaction mutex). This avoids unnecessary cloning.  
     - `NFT_ITER_READ` handler unchanged.

   - In `nft_rhash_walk()`, added `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` alongside `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` in the condition that skips resetting `iter->skip` (since both are update-type operations). Only `NFT_ITER_READ` resets `skip`.

- The core idea is to **restrict set cloning to the flush command only** to avoid unnecessary memory allocations and the resulting WARN splat when allocation fails during other operations (e.g., map deactivation).  
- A new iterator type **`NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`** is introduced specifically for the flush path.  
- The flush function (`nft_set_flush`) is the sole user of this new type, ensuring cloning only happens there.  
- Backend implementations (`rbtree`, `pipapo`) are updated to clone only when this type is used; otherwise they work on the existing set (or its clone if already cloned).  
- The hash backend simply treats `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` identically to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` (since rhashtable does not need explicit cloning).  
- The map deactivation path (`nft_map_deactivate`) retains `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to avoid cloning in contexts where the set is being destroyed or the clone already exists.  
- This separation ensures that **cloning is limited to the preparation phase of flush**, preventing memory allocation failures from causing warnings in other code paths.

Restrict set clone to the flush set command in the preparation phase.
Add NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE and use it for this purpose, update the rbtree
and pipapo backends to only clone the set when this iteration type is
used.

As for the existing NFT_ITER_UPDATE type, update the pipapo backend to
use the existing set clone if available, otherwise use the existing set
representation. After this update, there is no need to clone a set that
is being deleted, this includes bound anonymous set.

An alternative approach to NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE is to add a .clone
interface and call it from the flush set path.

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications per file

- **include/net/netfilter/nf_tables.h**  
  Added `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` to the `nft_iter_type` enum, with a comment indicating that the set should be cloned before iteration under the mutex for update operations.

- **net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c**  
  - Added explanatory comment in `nft_map_deactivate()` to clarify that it continues to use `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` (not `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`) because the set may already have a clone or may be going away (no cloning needed).  
  - In `nft_set_flush()`, changed the iteration type from `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` so that the set is cloned during the preparation phase of a flush command. This ensures cloning only occurs when needed (flush), avoiding unnecessary memory allocations in other update paths.

- **net/netfilter/nft_set_pipapo.c**  
  - In `nft_pipapo_walk()`, added a new `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` that calls `pipapo_maybe_clone()` (cloning the set) and, on failure, sets `iter->err = -ENOMEM`.  
  - Modified the existing `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to use the already existing clone (`priv->clone`) if available, otherwise fall back to the live set (`rcu_dereference_protected`). Previously it always attempted to clone; now cloning is only done for `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`.

- **net/netfilter/nft_set_hash.c**  
  - In `nft_rhash_walk()`, added `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` alongside the existing `case NFT_ITER_UPDATE`. Both cases only emit a warning if `iter->skip` is non-zero; no cloning is required for the hash backend.

- **net/netfilter/nft_set_rbtree.c**  
  - In `nft_rbtree_walk()`, split the original `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` case:  
    - `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE` performs the memory resize check (`nft_array_may_resize()`) and returns an error if it fails, then falls through to `NFT_ITER_UPDATE`.  
    - `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` now only acquires the lockdep assertion and proceeds to walk the set directly, without attempting resizing.  
  - This ensures that the potentially failing resize (allocation) is only attempted when the caller explicitly requests a clone (flush).

### Relationships among modifications

The core idea is to decouple “cloning the set” from “iteration under update lock” by introducing a new iteration type (`NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`).  
- The flush command (`nft_set_flush()`) now uses this new type, triggering the backend to clone the set if necessary during the preparation phase.  
- The pipapo backend was the primary source of the bug because it unconditionally cloned on every `NFT_ITER_UPDATE`, including paths where cloning was not required (e.g., netlink release). The fix moves cloning to the new type and allows `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` to reuse an existing clone or the live set.  
- The rbtree backend similarly moves the resizing (which can fail) to the new type, preventing unnecessary memory pressure.  
- The hash backend does not require cloning, so both types are handled identically.  
- A comment in `nft_map_deactivate()` clarifies why `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` (without clone) is still appropriate for deactivation paths.  

Overall, the patch restricts cloning to the flush operation, reducing the risk of memory allocation failures in other contexts while maintaining correctness for flush.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the pipapo set backend unconditionally clones the set (via `pipapo_maybe_clone`) during `NFT_ITER_UPDATE` iteration, even when cloning is unnecessary (e.g., during netlink release or deactivation). This allocation with `GFP_KERNEL` fails under memory pressure, triggering a WARN splat in `nft_map_deactivate`. The fix restricts cloning to only the flush command by introducing `NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE`.

 {
 	struct nft_pipapo *priv = nft_set_priv(set);
 	const struct nft_pipapo_match *m;
 
 	switch (iter->type) {
-	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE:
 		m = pipapo_maybe_clone(set);
 		if (!m) {

 			return;

-

+	case NFT_ITER_UPDATE:
+		if (priv->clone)
+			m = priv->clone;
+		else
+			m = rcu_dereference_protected(priv->match,
+						      nft_pipapo_transaction_mutex_held(set));
 		nft_pipapo_do_walk(ctx, set, m, iter);
 		break;
 	case NFT_ITER_READ:
 		rcu_read_lock();
 		m = rcu_dereference(priv->match);
 		nft_pipapo_do_walk(ctx, set, m, iter);
 		rcu_read_unlock();
 		break;
 	default:
 		iter->err = -EINVAL;
 		WARN_ON_ONCE(1);
 		break;
 	}
 }
